item.title: Sep 7 — 2 papers
item.description:
Two papers on making control decisions under explicit uncertainty budgets: the first recasts each rule in a driving rulebook as a risk measure with its own threshold, then solves the resulting lexicographic problem by branch-and-bound to return a policy together with a certified optimality gap. The second trains a JEPA-style world model that jointly predicts a robot's future state and the wireless channel's future condition from camera frames and radio spectrograms, using those coupled predictions to drop uplink transmissions when the model expects control quality to hold.

  1. Risk-Aware Optimal Control with Rulebooks — Tichakorn Wongpiromsarn
    It takes rulebooks, the ranked list of driving rules idea, and makes each rule a risk measure with a threshold, then solves the resulting lexicographic problem with a branch-and-bound routine that hands you a policy plus a certified bound on how far from optimal it might be.
  2. Coupled Control and Wireless World Models for Resilient Remote Robotic Control — H. P. Madushanka, Sumudu Samarakoon, Mehdi Bennis
    They train a JEPA-style world model that predicts both a robot's future state and the wireless channel's future condition from camera images plus radio spectrograms, and use those joint predictions to decide when the robot can skip an uplink transmission without losing control quality.
